questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

In this question, give all answers correct to two decimal places.

Sam invests $1700 in a savings account that pays a nominal annual rate of interest of 2.74%, compounded half-yearly. Sam makes no further payments to, or withdrawals from, this account.

(a) Find the amount that Sam will have in his account after 10 years. [3]

David also invests $1700 in a savings account that pays an annual rate of interest of r%, compounded yearly. David makes no further payments or withdrawals from this account.

(b) Find the value of r required so that the amount in David’s account after 10 years will be equal to the amount in Sam’s account. [2]

(c) Find the interest David will earn over the 10 years. [1]
questions.summary: Compare half-yearly and yearly compound interest.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 4]

The number of hours spent exercising each week by a group of students is shown in the following table.

[Table: Exercising time (in hours): 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Corresponding number of students: 5, 1, 4, 3, x.]

The median is 4.5 hours.

(a) Find the value of x. [2]

(b) Find the standard deviation. [2]
questions.summary: Use a frequency table, median and standard deviation.
questions.solution: (a) For median 4.5, the middle pair is 4 and 5, requiring 20 values; hence x=7. (b) Using frequencies 5,1,4,3,7 gives population standard deviation 1.58429…, so 1.58 hours.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

A company is designing a new logo. The logo is created by removing two equal segments from a rectangle, as shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram not to scale: The logo is a shaded rectangle whose left and right sides have identical inward-facing circular-arc cut-outs.]

The rectangle measures 5 cm by 4 cm. The points A and B lie on a circle, with centre O and radius 2 cm, such that AÔB = θ, where 0 < θ < π. This information is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram not to scale: A rectangle has horizontal width 4 and vertical height 5. Its left and right inward circular segments are shaded. On the left, A and B are the upper and lower endpoints of the segment’s vertical chord; O lies outside the rectangle to their left. Radii OA and OB are each 2 and enclose the central angle θ at O. The right segment is congruent and mirrored.]

(a) Find the area of one of the shaded segments in terms of θ. [3]

(b) Given that the area of the logo is 13.4 cm², find the value of θ. [3]
questions.summary: Use sector and triangle areas for circular segments.
questions.solution: (a) Segment area=(1/2)(2²)θ−(1/2)(2²)sinθ=2θ−2sinθ. (b) 20−2(2θ−2sinθ)=13.4. Solving 2θ−2sinθ=3.3 gives θ=2.35672…=2.36 radians.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

A discrete random variable, X, has the following probability distribution:

[Table: x: 0, 1, 2, 3. Corresponding P(X = x): 0.41, k − 0.28, 0.46, 0.29 − 2k².]

(a) Show that 2k² − k + 0.12 = 0. [1]

(b) Find the value of k, giving a reason for your answer. [3]

(c) Hence, find E(X). [2]
questions.summary: Determine a probability parameter and expectation.
questions.solution: (a) Summing probabilities to 1 gives 2k²−k+0.12=0. (b) Roots are 0.2 and 0.3; k=0.2 makes P(X=1)<0, so k=0.3. (c) E(X)=1(0.02)+2(0.46)+3(0.11)=1.27.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

A particle moves along a straight line so that its velocity, v m s⁻¹, after t seconds is given by v(t) = e^(sin t) + 4 sin t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6.

(a) Find the value of t when the particle is at rest. [2]

(b) Find the acceleration of the particle when it changes direction. [3]

(c) Find the total distance travelled by the particle. [2]
questions.solution: (a) Solve e^(sin t)+4sin t=0: t=3.34692…=3.35 s. (b) a=v′=cos t[e^(sin t)+4], so at this time a=−4.71439…=−4.71 m s⁻². (c) Split ∫|v| at 3.34692; the two distances are 14.3104… and 6.44300…, totaling 20.8 m.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

Let A and B be two independent events such that P(A ∩ B′) = 0.16 and P(A′ ∩ B) = 0.36.

(a) Given that P(A ∩ B) = x, find the value of x. [4]

(b) Find P(A′ | B′). [2]
questions.summary: Use independence in a probability partition.
questions.solution: P(A)=x+0.16 and P(B)=x+0.36. Independence gives x=(x+0.16)(x+0.36), whose valid solution is x=0.24. (b) Independence is preserved under complements, so P(A′|B′)=P(A′)=1−(0.24+0.16)=0.6.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 13]

All lengths in this question are in centimetres.

A solid metal ornament is in the shape of a right pyramid, with vertex V and square base ABCD. The centre of the base is X. Point V has coordinates (1, 5, 0) and point A has coordinates (−1, 1, 6).

[Diagram not to scale: A right square-based pyramid has apex V and base vertices A, B, C and D. The base centre X is marked. Dashed segments show VD, VX and the hidden base edges AD and DC; VX is the perpendicular height from V to the centre of the square base.]

(a) Find AV. [2]

(b) Given that ∠AVB = 40°, find AB. [3]

The volume of the pyramid is 57.2 cm³, correct to three significant figures.

(c) Find the height of the pyramid, VX. [3]

A second ornament is in the shape of a cuboid with a rectangular base of length 2x cm, width x cm and height y cm. The cuboid has the same volume as the pyramid.

(d) The cuboid has a minimum surface area of S cm². Find the value of S. [5]
questions.summary: Apply 3D distance, trigonometry, volume and optimization.
questions.solution: (a) AV=√[2²+4²+(−6)²]=√56=7.48. (b) Isosceles triangle AVB gives AB=2AV sin20°=5.12. (c) 57.2=(1/3)AB²(VX), hence VX=6.55. (d) 2x²y=57.2, so y=28.6/x². Surface area S=2[(2x)(x)+(2x)y+xy]=4x²+6xy=4x²+171.6/x. Minimization gives x=2.77849… and S=92.6 cm².

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

The function f is defined by f(x) = (4x + 1)/(x + 4), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ −4.

(a) For the graph of f

(i) write down the equation of the vertical asymptote;

(ii) find the equation of the horizontal asymptote. [3]

(b) (i) Find f⁻¹(x).

(ii) Using an algebraic approach, show that the graph of f⁻¹ is obtained by a reflection of the graph of f in the y-axis followed by a reflection in the x-axis. [8]

The graphs of f and f⁻¹ intersect at x = p and x = q, where p < q.

(c) (i) Find the value of p and the value of q.

(ii) Hence, find the area enclosed by the graph of f and the graph of f⁻¹. [5]
questions.summary: Analyze a rational function and its inverse.
questions.solution: (a) x=−4; y=4. (b)(i) Interchanging x,y and solving gives f⁻¹(x)=(1−4x)/(x−4). (ii) −f(−x)=−[(−4x+1)/(−x+4)]=(1−4x)/(x−4)=f⁻¹(x), exactly the stated two reflections. (c)(i) Solving f(x)=x gives x=−1,1, so p=−1,q=1. (ii) ∫₋₁¹[f(x)−f⁻¹(x)]dx=0.675231…=0.675 square units.

9. [Maximum mark: 16]

A bakery makes two types of muffins: chocolate muffins and banana muffins.

The weights, C grams, of the chocolate muffins are normally distributed with a mean of 62 g and standard deviation of 2.9 g.

(a) Find the probability that a randomly selected chocolate muffin weighs less than 61 g. [2]

(b) In a random selection of 12 chocolate muffins, find the probability that exactly 5 weigh less than 61 g. [2]

The weights, B grams, of the banana muffins are normally distributed with a mean of 68 g and standard deviation of 3.4 g.

Each day 60% of the muffins made are chocolate.

On a particular day, a muffin is randomly selected from all those made at the bakery.

(c) (i) Find the probability that the randomly selected muffin weighs less than 61 g.

(ii) Given that a randomly selected muffin weighs less than 61 g, find the probability that it is chocolate. [7]

The machine that makes the chocolate muffins is adjusted so that the mean weight of the chocolate muffins remains the same but their standard deviation changes to σ g. The machine that makes the banana muffins is not adjusted. The probability that the weight of a randomly selected muffin from these machines is less than 61 g is now 0.157.

(d) Find the value of σ. [5]
questions.summary: Combine normal, binomial and conditional probabilities.
